description: Start a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance: find companies on the web that match a plain-language description, and collect each one's public contact data. Returns a task_id at once, with the task's status and reserved_cost_usd. Cost: the call reserves count companies at the Company Search per-company price at the time of the call (reserved_cost_usd; prices at https://desearch.ai/pricing). When the task ends you pay only for the companies it delivered (final_cost_usd; a minimum of 2 when it delivers any; a task that delivers none is free) and the rest of the reservation is returned. A company left out by min_score or require is not billed. Each company has a fit score (0-100) and why it matched, plus fully_verified and unverified_criteria (what its own pages do and do not confirm). Data: Desearch reads public data only: each company's own website (its homepage and its contact, about, team, and imprint pages), public web search results, and public LinkedIn profiles of its leaders. Each company comes back with its location, public emails, phones, and social profiles, and its leaders (roles) with their title, LinkedIn profile, and emails. Every contact keeps the page it came from (source_url). Leader emails can be inferred from the company's address pattern (source: inferred, with a confidence), and every email is checked (verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown). Companies stay readable for 30 days after the task ends. The task runs in the background: poll company-search-status with the task_id to read progress and the companies delivered so far. Each company is delivered first with enrichment status partial, and the later stages (contact pages, leaders, inferred emails, email checks) fill it in until it is complete. Use company-search-pause, company-search-resume, or company-search-cancel to pause, resume, or cancel it. Do not start the same task twice; send idempotency_key so a retry returns the first task instead of charging again. To read companies you already know by domain, use company-enrich instead.

count.description: How many companies to deliver (5-200, API default 25). The task reserves this many and bills only the companies it delivers.

countries.description: Where the companies should be: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes or country names, example: ['DE', 'Austria'] (up to 20). Scoring treats them as a location criterion. Sent as filters.countries.

exclude.description: Companies to leave out, as domains or URLs, for example ones you already contacted (up to 1000). Each is reduced to its host without www.

idempotency_key.description: Any unique string for this task, for example a UUID. Sending the same key again returns the first task and is not charged again.

infer_emails.description: Guess leaders' emails from the company's address pattern (for example first.last), learned from the addresses found on its site (API default true). Inferred emails say source: inferred and carry a confidence: high when the pattern was learned from this company's own addresses, low for a common pattern.

metadata.description: Your own labels for this task, example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}. Up to 10 keys; keys are 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9, '_', '.', '-'; values are strings of up to 200 characters. Returned on the task; filter company-search-tasks by it. The task does not use it.

min_score.description: Only deliver companies with at least this fit score (0-100).

query.description: The companies you are looking for, in plain language: what they do, where, how far along. Example: 'Series A fintech startups in Berlin building payment infrastructure'.

require.description: Only deliver companies that have all of these: 'email', 'phone', 'linkedin' (the company's LinkedIn page), 'leader' (one of roles), 'leader_email' (a leader with an email). A company is delivered once the stage that can show them has run (email, phone, linkedin: the contact pages; leader: the leaders; leader_email: the email checks); one that does not have them is not delivered and not billed. Sent as filters.require.

roles.description: The leaders to look for: any of 'ceo', 'founder', 'cto', 'cfo', 'coo', 'cmo', 'president', 'owner', 'managing_director' (API default ['ceo', 'founder', 'cto', 'cfo']). A managing director (Geschäftsführer) counts as 'ceo' when 'ceo' is asked for.

verify_emails.description: Check every email: syntax, mail server (MX) and, for inferred ones, a web search (API default true). Each email then has a verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown. Set false to finish sooner without it.

name: company-search
title: Company Search
